A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and benchmark experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and token-usage experiments across five benchmarks and five models, answer-convergence measurements, and a manual faithfulness analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds accuracy and token-usage measurements for two hyperparameter sweeps in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The three procedures remain unchanged: consecutive-answer consistency, end-of-reasoning logit boosting, and the activation-based LSTM stopping predictor. Their inputs, training labels, loss, and stopping rules are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, GSM8K, MATH-500, GPQA-Diamond, and AIME’24. The added sensitivity experiments reuse these tasks without introducing new domains, populations, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The original model and Concise CoT remain the evaluated baselines in Figure 3. v2 discusses DEER as concurrent work but reports no experimental comparison against it.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds controlled sweeps on R1-distilled-Llama3.1-8B: alpha from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.2, and k in {2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30}. Existing dataset splits, metrics, training settings, and main-experiment defaults of alpha = 0.6 and k = 10 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic sensitivity analyses of both unsupervised stopping controls across all five benchmarks, examining premature stopping and accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs in Tables 3–6. These analyses were absent from v1. The existing faithfulness study moves from Section 7 to Appendix A.6 without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions already state in Appendix A.3 that experiments are run three times and averaged. v2 repeats this statement in A.4 but adds no seeds, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All main Figure 3 values are retained, but v2 adds substantial accuracy/token grids establishing dependence on the two stopping parameters. For example, GSM8K accuracy rises from 15.6% at k = 2 to 78.4% at k = 30, with tokens increasing from 65.6 to 396.1. Some new default-setting entries disagree with the retained main results: AIME’24 tokens at alpha = 0.6 are 2429.8 in Table 4 versus 3571.2 in Figure 3, without explanation.

T1.justification: The Answer Convergence Ratio definition, logit transformation, stopping classifier, and binary cross-entropy objective are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces a broad statement that early stopping preserves accuracy with method-specific assertions: Learn-to-Stop maintains accuracy across simple and complex tasks, while unsupervised methods provide efficiency gains particularly on simpler datasets. The central answer-convergence contribution and abstract/conclusion claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds explanations of premature termination and practical recommendations for alpha and k. New Section 7 links larger-model token savings to more confident convergence, extending the model-capacity interpretation already present in v1 Appendix A.1. Existing correctness and faithfulness limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract footnote pointing to a Hugging Face project page for additional details and documents the model and parameter grids used for the new sweeps. Existing implementation settings and prompt templates are retained; the PDFs do not establish the contents of the linked resource.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2025), Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models, and positions its consistency and learned stopping signals as complementary to DEER’s confidence-based approach. It condenses the earlier literature review and removes the dedicated latent-reasoning paragraph, while retaining those citations elsewhere.

P1.justification: Related Work is condensed, introductory wording is revised, and the faithfulness section moves to Appendix A.6 while Section 7 becomes a model-size discussion. Most methodological and results prose is retained, so the restructuring is localized.

P2.justification: v2 adds four conventional sensitivity tables and relocates existing displays. The faithfulness chart moves to the appendix, the convergence figure is renumbered, and case tables and prompts are rearranged. Existing plots and the main results display retain their substantive visual structure.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity studies make the stopping parameters’ accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs more assessable, and the DEER discussion improves research positioning. These are useful additions to an otherwise stable paper. The gain is limited by unexplained inconsistencies between new appendix entries and retained main results, including 2429.8 versus 3571.2 AIME’24 tokens at the stated alpha = 0.6 setting; consequently, the added evidence does not support a substantial overall quality improvement.
